title: Adaptive micro-batching with tenant-priority soft quotas and ephemeral model sandboxes for OOM resilience
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Implement an adaptive micro-batching layer that enforces tenant-priority soft quotas and spins up ephemeral model sandboxes for degraded retries. The goal is to reduce OOM incidence and improve graceful degradation under transient high concurrency without impacting high-priority tenants. Key pieces: predictive admission controller, per-tenant soft quota accounting, micro-batch contraction (token-window aware), KV cache checkpointing to host for cold/evicted prefixes, and ephemeral low-fidelity model sandboxes for fast fallback retries. The solution must integrate with runtime admission, autoscaler signals, and the existing KV lease coordinator.

Scope (MVP):
- Admission controller that computes expected memory delta for an incoming micro-batch using recent sequence length histograms per-tenant and per-route.
- Soft quotas per-tenant that allow temporary overcommit with a short backoff window before hard denial.
- Micro-batch contraction: algorithm to split/trim a batch into prioritized sub-batches under memory pressure.
- KV checkpoint snapshots to host memory for cold prefixes and graceful recomposition when pressure subsides.
- Ephemeral model sandbox: an in-memory lightweight model variant (quantized / distilled) spun up pre-warmed to accept retries for requests evicted from main model due to memory constraints.

Non-goals: full multitenant billing rework, new hardware drivers, persistent datastore changes beyond KV host checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary: rollout to 10% of runtime fleet with two canary tenants (internal) and no more than 2% increase in P95 token latency for those tenants.
OOM rate in synthetic stress test (20x baseline concurrency) reduced by >= 90% compared to baseline without microbatching and ephemeral sandboxes.
Telemetry: new metrics (admission.rejected, admission.trimmed_batches, kv.checkpointed_prefixes, sandbox.fallbacks) show expected events and are emitted to observability pipelines.
Fallback correctness: requests retried to ephemeral sandboxes return syntactically valid outputs and are tagged in traces with fallback reason.
Graceful degradation: high-priority tenant SLOs maintained during pressure windows while low-priority tenants observe controlled backoff and retry policy.
